question: In 1984 the quagga became the first extinct animal to have its DNA read. What did genetics eventually show it was?
options: A close cousin of the horse
answer: A form of plains zebra. Fragments from a museum skin placed it among the zebras, and later work put it inside the plains zebra, differing mainly in coat. That is why a South African project has, since 1987, bred ordinary plains zebras for fewer stripes and browner backs, producing animals that look like quaggas.
move: Looks can divide what ancestry joins; check the ancestry.
trap: A half-striped brown coat looks too different to be the same zebra.
reference: Higuchi, Bowman, Freiberger, Ryder & Wilson, DNA sequences from the quagga, an extinct member of the horse family, Nature, 1984
